text:
May the mind contemplate, not delight in this fleeting, stone‑like existence, which is bound by belief.  
May the king’s crown, the crown of the Brahmin’s head, the wandering merchants, the traders, the servants, the limbs, the throats, the ears, the eyes, the noses, the mouths, the hands, the feet, the eyes, the ears, the noses, the mouths, the hands, the feet—may all these be entered, O ruler of Varanasi, through the doors of the house.  
We stand in line, having fallen from the vessel of the hand, and we seek alms.
